subject: API: intermittent 504s impacting Helion connector
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@helion.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@helionsys.com
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: API: intermittent 504s impacting Helion connector

Marcus —

We started seeing intermittent 504s between 08:50 and 09:10 PDT this morning (peak failure rate ~12%). The failures are concentrated on the /v1/generate endpoint when requests include interactive streaming. This is triggering downstream job retries on our side and pushing our SLA into breach territory for the third consecutive week.

I attached a small log bundle and a short extract of our SLA report for the window. Can Redwood confirm whether there were any deploys, autoscaler events, or model swaps in our region during the window? We need an initial root-cause hypothesis and a mitigation plan within 24 hours; Helion needs either a temporary routing fallback or a hotfix.

If we can't get a reliable plan quickly we will have to pause the integration on our side, which will materially affect our customers.

Thanks —
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Integrations
Helion Systems

Attachments: helion_log_bundle_0614.zip, helion-sla-extract.pdf

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@helion.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API: intermittent 504s impacting Helion connector

Jane —

Thanks for the report and the logs. Really sorry for the disruption. We're opening an ops bridge and triage ticket (JIRA-OPS-4521) now and I'll be lead on coordination. Quick answers up front: no user-facing deploys were scheduled in your region this morning, but the autoscaler did record a short GPU pool reclaim for slot balancing at 08:49 PDT — engineering is already looking into whether that coincides with a cache eviction path.

Immediate next steps (proposal):
- 10:30 PDT: 30m ops bridge with Helion and Redwood partner ops (I'll send invite)
- Engineering to run targeted request replay from the logs you provided to reproduce the 504s
- Temporary mitigation: if reproducer confirms a model-variant timeout, we'll gate Helion to the previous stable variant for 24–48 hours
- If gating not sufficient, enable request-level retry guard with jitter and a higher timeout for your routes

Can you confirm the most critical customer-facing routes so we can prioritize the replay? Also accept the bridge invite and share any additional traces (request IDs) if available.

I'm CC'ing Sergio for oncall/runbook actions and Marissa for CS escalation and credit discussion.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Partner Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@helion.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API: intermittent 504s impacting Helion connector

Thanks Marcus and Jane —

We ran the initial replay against the logs Jane attached. Observations so far:
- A subset of requests hit a rare KV-cache thrash path when sequence lengths exceeded our 1k token warm threshold; that combined with a transient autoscaler reclaim produced synchronous backpressure and 504s for streaming sessions.
- The issue is reproducible in our staging replay when we mimic Helion's burst pattern.

Immediate fixes we can implement:
1) Gate Helion's production traffic to the previous model variant (stable-2026-05-01) — low risk and fast (5–10m).
2) Apply a guard in the request router to increase request timeout to 65s for streaming routes from Helion (config change, no deploy).
3) Engineering will push a targeted cache eviction mitigation next 24–36h; ETA for deploy: 36–48h.

Requesting Helion sign-off on option 1+2 for an 48h window so we can buy time for the cache fix. If Helion wants us to keep the current variant, we'll need to implement 2 immediately and monitor.

I'll open a short runbook note in Drive (see link below) and add the step-by-step to perform the rollback/gating and the rollback criteria.

On the support/contract side: Marissa, can you advise whether we should auto-apply a pro-rated SLA credit if downtime > 2 hours cumulative for Helion this month?

Sergio
Partner Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@helion.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API: intermittent 504s impacting Helion connector

Jane —

Thanks for the quick coordination and for confirming priority routes ("/v1/generate:stream" and the webhook callback path). Per today's bridge and Sergio's replay, Redwood will proceed with the following plan now that we have your approval:

1) Immediate action (now): gate Helion traffic to stable-2026-05-01 (expected impact <5 minutes).
2) Router guard: increase timeout to 65s for your streaming routes (effective immediately, no deploy).
3) Monitoring: we will run a 6h high-sensitivity monitor and report every hour to this thread.
4) Engineering patch: cache eviction mitigation targeted for 36–48h; we'll send a canary plan prior to the push.

Marissa: please initiate SLA credit evaluation for Helion under the terms in their contract and flag to finance if >2h cumulative impact. Ben: please stand by to assist if the rollback introduces any upgrade incompatibilities.

Jane, please confirm acceptance so we can execute gate+timeout now. If you prefer a different window, note in your reply.

Appreciate the patience — we'll work to restore normal behaviour and follow up with a postmortem once engineering has the fix deployed.

—Marcus
Sr. Partner Success Manager
Redwood Inference
